help.intro: A weekend at grandma's with twelve gaps that ask for the two big things of this module at once: the Perfekt helper — habe or bin, hat or sind — and the dative article after mit, bei and nach. Every gap has a hint that names only the pieces (the subject and the infinitive, or the preposition and the noun with its article: mit · der Zug); the decision — haben or sein, which case — is yours. Read the whole text first, because the participle at the end of each sentence tells you which helper the gap needs, and the noun after each preposition tells you its gender. Then work through it in order: helpers, then articles. One gap is not Perfekt at all: Das Wetter war schön — a state, told with war.
help.tips[0].title: Read to the participle before choosing the helper
help.tips[0].text: Read to the participle before choosing the helper: 'ich ____ am Samstagmorgen mit dem Zug gefahren' — gefahren is movement, so bin. 'Letztes Wochenende ____ ich meine Oma besucht' — besucht has an object, so habe.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I went by train on Saturday morning.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Last weekend I visited my grandma.
help.tips[0].check.q: Am Sonntag ____ wir nach Hause gefahren.
help.tips[0].check.why: The participle gefahren is movement from one place to another, so the helper is sein; with wir it is sind.
help.tips[1].text: mit dem Zug (der Zug), bei der Oma (die Oma), nach dem Essen (das Essen). The hint gives the noun with its article; the preposition tells you the case — and mit, bei and nach always take the same one.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: At grandma's I first ate cake.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: After the meal we went for a walk in the park.
help.tips[1].trap: 'mit den Bus' (accusative) is the beginner's reflex. mit is dative: dem.
help.tips[1].check.q: Oma ist mit ____ Bus gekommen. (der Bus)
help.tips[1].check.why: mit always takes the dative, and masculine der becomes dem.
help.tips[2].title: Two sentences are states: war
help.tips[2].text: Das Wetter war schön. Es war ein schöner Tag. Weather and the summary of a day are states, so they take war, not the Perfekt.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The weather was nice, and we talked for a long time.
help.tips[2].check.why: Weather in the past is a state, so German simply uses war, not a Perfekt.
help.remember[0]: Participle first (it's at the end), helper second (it's in the gap).
help.remember[1]: mit, bei, nach: dative, every time.
help.hook: Retell a weekend at grandma's: pick bin or habe, dem or der, and your story sounds like real German.
passageTranslation: Last weekend I visited my grandma. She lives in Bonn, and I went by train on Saturday morning. The journey took only an hour. At the station my grandma was waiting for me. We walked to her flat together. At grandma's I first ate cake – she bakes the best apple cake! Then she showed me old photos. In one photo was my father as a child. After the meal we went for a walk in the park. The weather was nice, and we talked for a long time. In the evening I went home by bus. It was a lovely day.
inlineBlanks[0].why: besuchen takes an object (meine Oma), so the Perfekt uses haben: ich habe besucht.
inlineBlanks[1].why: fahren is movement from A to B, so the Perfekt uses sein: ich bin gefahren.
inlineBlanks[2].why: mit always takes the dative. Zug is masculine, so der becomes dem: mit dem Zug.
inlineBlanks[3].why: dauern is not movement or change, so the Perfekt uses haben. Die Fahrt is 'it': hat gedauert.
inlineBlanks[4].why: laufen here is movement to a place, so the Perfekt uses sein. With wir: sind gelaufen.
inlineBlanks[5].why: bei always takes the dative. Oma is feminine, so die becomes der: bei der Oma.
inlineBlanks[6].why: essen takes an object (Kuchen), so the Perfekt uses haben: ich habe gegessen.
inlineBlanks[7].why: zeigen takes an object (Fotos), so the Perfekt uses haben. With sie (she): hat gezeigt.
inlineBlanks[8].why: nach always takes the dative. Essen is neuter, so das becomes dem: nach dem Essen.
inlineBlanks[9].why: spazieren gehen is movement, so the Perfekt uses sein. With wir: sind spazieren gegangen.
inlineBlanks[10].why: For sein, German uses the simple past (Präteritum) in stories. das Wetter is 'it': war.
inlineBlanks[11].why: fahren is movement (nach Hause), so the Perfekt uses sein: ich bin gefahren.
help.tips[1].title: mit / bei / nach → dem, der, dem
